about.name: Arush Ugal
about.title: Backend Software Engineer
about.summary: Backend software engineer specializing in REST API design and distributed systems. I build high-throughput, low-latency backend infrastructure for core financial transaction pipelines and payment systems, applying concurrency and fault-tolerant patterns to keep services fast and reliable at scale. I care about clean service boundaries, resilient architectures, and APIs that stay performant for millions of daily users.

descriptionPoints: Selected from a pool of 5,000+ candidates through rigorous data-structures, algorithms, and systems-design interview rounds.

Engineered high-throughput, low-latency backend infrastructure for core financial transaction pipelines, leveraging distributed systems and concurrency patterns to ensure fault tolerance under heavy load.
Optimized payment gateway REST APIs for sub-second execution and horizontal scalability, sustaining reliable performance for millions of daily active users.

projects.title: HireMeNow — AI Recruitment Platform
descriptionPoints: Designed, built, and deployed a production SaaS platform using React 18 + TypeScript, a Node.js/Express backend, and Firebase Firestore, hosted on Vercel and Railway.
Built an AI-powered resume parsing engine that automatically extracts 40+ structured attributes from candidate resumes.
Implemented real-time candidate matching over Socket.io with sub-second latency for live recruiter feedback.
Integrated Twilio Video for in-app interviews and Firebase Auth with Google OAuth for secure sign-in.
Established a CI/CD pipeline that sustained 99.9% uptime across production deployments.

projects.title: Quantitative Time-Series Data Pipeline
descriptionPoints: Built an automated data pipeline that ingests a decade of live market pricing data for quantitative analysis.
Developed a 3-sigma anomaly-detection engine to flag statistically significant price movements.
Packaged the workflow into a fully reproducible, containerized dashboard that regenerates end-to-end in under 60 seconds.

projects.title: PROJECT SPYN — Autonomous Embedded Navigation
descriptionPoints: Implemented real-time embedded control fusing gyroscope and bump-sensor data across 28 iterative build cycles.
Stress-tested 8 distinct navigation models to validate autonomous pathing under varied conditions.
Led hardware-software integration across a 5-person team to deliver a working autonomous navigation system.
